# lucidity_temp_buffer (Resource)

A temporary storage buffer on one Lucidity-managed instance, e.g. extra free space for a database restore or data migration. Creating it requests the buffer and waits until it is ACTIVE; destroying it revokes the buffer and returns the instance to its original scaling policy. A buffer keeps incurring cloud storage cost until it is revoked — Lucidity does not revoke it automatically. Only one buffer can be active per instance. Lucidity's API has no call to resize or modify a buffer, so changing the size or the instance revokes the buffer and requests a new one — don't change them while an operation depends on the buffer, and don't use create_before_destroy (the new request would conflict with the old buffer). Keep buffer_id (e.g. as an output): Lucidity returns it only once, and it is the import ID.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Adds 50 GiB of temporary free space to a Lucidity-managed instance, e.g.
# before a database restore. `terraform apply` requests the buffer and waits
# until it is ACTIVE; `terraform destroy` (or removing the block) revokes it.
# The buffer keeps costing money until it is revoked.
resource "lucidity_temp_buffer" "orders_db_restore" {
  instance_identifier {
    cloud_provider            = "AWS"
    cloud_provider_account_id = "123456789012"
    instance_id               = "i-0abcd1234efgh5678"
  }

  request_buffer_size_in_gib = 50
  request_id                 = "restore-orders-db-2026-10-23" # optional; generated if omitted
}

# Azure needs the resource group, and instance_id may be the VM name.
resource "lucidity_temp_buffer" "azure_vm" {
  instance_identifier {
    cloud_provider            = "AZURE"
    cloud_provider_account_id = "a1b2c3d4-5678-90ef-1234-3456abcdef01"
    instance_id               = "my-vm-instance"
    resource_group            = "my-resource-group"
  }

  request_buffer_size_in_gib = 100
}

# Only hold the buffer while a restore is planned: flip the variable to true
# before the restore and back to false afterwards to revoke it.
variable "restore_in_progress" {
  type    = bool
  default = false
}

resource "lucidity_temp_buffer" "on_demand" {
  count = var.restore_in_progress ? 1 : 0

  instance_identifier {
    cloud_provider            = "GCP"
    cloud_provider_account_id = "my-gcp-project-id"
    instance_id               = "gcp-instance-12345"
  }

  request_buffer_size_in_gib = 75
}

# Lucidity returns the buffer ID only once. Terraform keeps it in state; also
# expose it if a restore script or a later `terraform import` needs it.
output "orders_db_restore_buffer_id" {
  value = lucidity_temp_buffer.orders_db_restore.buffer_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `request_buffer_size_in_gib` (Number) Size of the temporary buffer, in GiB. Lucidity's docs say buffers typically range from 1 GiB to 1 TiB; limits vary by cloud provider and instance type.

### Optional

- `instance_identifier` (Block, Optional) The instance to add the buffer to. Required. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--instance_identifier))
- `request_id` (String) Client-generated ID Lucidity uses to deduplicate the buffer request, so a retried request never creates a second buffer. Generated automatically if not set. Set it yourself to make it descriptive and stable (e.g. "restore-orders-db-2026-10-23"): if an apply fails after Lucidity received the request, re-applying with the same request_id gets the same buffer back instead of a conflict. Must be unique per buffer. Only used when the buffer is requested, so changing it later updates state only and leaves the existing buffer alone.

### Read-Only

- `buffer_id` (String) Lucidity's identifier for the buffer, saved to state as soon as Lucidity returns it. Lucidity returns it only once and has no way to look it up later, so keep it (e.g. as an output) if anything outside this configuration needs it. Also the import ID.
- `current_free_space_in_gib` (Number) Current free space reported for the buffer, in GiB.
- `failure_reason` (String) Why the buffer failed, when status is FAILED.
- `status` (String) PROVISIONING, ACTIVE, REVOKED, or FAILED.

<a id="nestedblock--instance_identifier"></a>
### Nested Schema for `instance_identifier`

Required:

- `cloud_provider` (String) AWS, AZURE, or GCP.
- `cloud_provider_account_id` (String) The cloud account that owns the instance: the AWS account ID (12 digits), the Azure subscription ID, or the GCP project ID.
- `instance_id` (String) The instance's ID (in Azure, this may be the VM name). Must be an instance Lucidity already manages.

Optional:

- `resource_group` (String) AZURE only, and required there: the resource group the VM is in.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import ID is the buffer ID Lucidity returned when the buffer was requested.
terraform import lucidity_temp_buffer.example buf-abc123def456
```
